# Mailloop subscriptions — implementation plan

Planning audit: 13 October 2026. **This document is a proposal. No application code, configuration, tests, packages, migrations, or database records were changed or executed for this task.** Local inspection was read-only. Dodo and Google references below were checked against their current official documentation. Dashboard settings, production infrastructure, and live provider behavior were not inspected.

## Decisions I need from you

| Decision                                                                      | Recommended default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Avoid restricted Gmail scopes, or ship automatic reply detection immediately? | Send-only v1; defer full reply tracking and reply-aware automatic follow-ups until a separately consented, verified read-access integration is ready. Do not advertise those deferred features as available. If the complete paid feature list is mandatory on day one, accept restricted-scope verification and assessment before launch. |
| Auto-follow-ups without automatic reply detection?                            | Do not enable by default. If offered before read access, require explicit acknowledgement that users must manually mark replies/opt-outs and automation cannot reliably stop on an unseen reply.                                                                                                                                           |
| Daily timezone                                                                | UTC, including free calendar-month boundaries; explain midnight UTC and show the equivalent local reset time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Failed-renewal grace                                                          | Three days, configured in Dodo and mirrored from its signed `past_due_ends_at` webhook field. No additional quota reset merely because grace starts.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Prices include tax?                                                           | Tax-inclusive ₹299/month for India and US$5.99/month globally, including applicable tax; verify hosted quotes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Existing users                                                                | 14-day transition with paid-equivalent feature limits, clearly labelled complimentary, followed by free. No permanent grandfathering or automatic charging.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Excess templates on downgrade                                                 | User selects one editable/usable template; oldest active template is the fallback. Others remain viewable/exportable, with edit/use locked.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Follow-up limits                                                              | At most two per original recipient, gaps of 3/7/14 elapsed days, default seven days, no sending after 30 days from the original email.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Account deletion retention                                                    | Disable sending immediately; cancel billing and revoke Google authorization promptly after draining workers; purge ordinary personal data within 30 days, backups within 35 additional days. Keep only legally required financial records separately. Replace the current 90-day policy.                                                   |

These are proposed defaults, not decisions already authorized for implementation. Section 14 adds the remaining choices and provider questions.

## 1. Current state audit

### Schema, tenancy, and infrastructure

`prisma/schema.prisma` contains the actual tables below. IDs use `String @id @default(uuid())`; PostgreSQL columns are presently string-backed rather than uniformly declared `@db.Uuid`. Preserve generated UUID identifiers and existing column types during this feature; do not mix incompatible FK types or opportunistically convert all IDs.

| Table             | Current model and implications                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `User`            | Unique `email`, nullable unique `googleId`, `encryptedRefreshToken`, `gmailAuthorized`, `preferredRoles`, `deletionRequestedAt`, `followUpDays` default 7, `nextSendAt`, `currentAttachmentId`, `createdAt`. No plan, subscription, administrator, suspension, or activity fields.                                                                 |
| `Template`        | Owner `userId`, name/subject/body, `archivedAt`, creation time; owner index. No template limit or read-only designation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Contact`         | Owner, name/email/company/jobRole/notes/tag; archive, shortlist-removal and manual follow-up timestamps. Unique `(userId,email)`; owner index. No durable do-not-contact suppression.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Campaign`        | Owner, template FK, string status/role, optional attachment FK, optional idempotency key. Unique `(userId,idempotencyKey)`; owner index.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Send`            | Campaign/contact FKs; immutable recipient/template/message snapshots; unique MIME Message-ID; Gmail message/thread IDs; queue/attempt/dispatch/check/sent timestamps. `SendStatus`: QUEUED/CANCELLED/SENT/FAILED/REPLIED. `DeliveryState`: READY/ATTEMPTING/UNCERTAIN/DONE. Ownership is reached through `campaign.userId`, not a direct `userId`. |
| `Attachment`      | Owner, filename, private storage path, deletion marker; campaigns preserve the row and protect pending files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `DeliveryReceipt` | Minimal owner/address/created/sent information retained when completed history is permanently deleted. Preserves quota and duplicate warnings; indexed by owner/time and owner/address.                                                                                                                                                            |

`package.json` pins Prisma client, adapter, and CLI to **7.10.0**, Next.js to **16.4.0**, Inngest to **4.22.0**, and Vercel Blob to **2.8.1**. `gmail-mime` aliases Nodemailer **10.0.16**, used to build MIME, not as an SMTP batch transport. No Dodo dependency exists. `src/lib/db.ts` uses `PrismaPg` with a five-connection pool. `prisma.config.ts` owns the connection configuration; client output is `src/generated/prisma`. `docker-compose.yml` runs PostgreSQL 16 on host port 5433; Next.js runs on the host. Preserve that arrangement.

Existing migrations cover roles/resumes, contact follow-up flags, launch controls, shortlist removal, and permanent history deletion. Especially preserve `prisma/migrations/20261012000000_permanent_history/migration.sql` semantics. A subscription feature must not resurrect deleted history.

### Authentication and scopes

`src/auth.ts` configures Auth.js Google OAuth with JWT sessions and requests:

```text
openid email profile
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly
```

It requests offline access and consent. `signIn` requires Google provider, verified email, `sub`, and no pending deletion. The `jwt` callback finds users by Google identity, rejects silently linking an unrelated email owner, locks existing users during updates, and encrypts newly returned refresh tokens. **`gmailAuthorized` becomes true only if both Gmail scopes were granted.** The session exposes the application user ID and invalidates access when deletion is pending; it does not put the refresh token into the session.

`src/lib/session.ts:requireUser()` authenticates and reloads the owner, rejecting pending deletion. It returns an internal object that includes the encrypted token. Existing pages pass derived booleans to clients; future billing/admin code must not spread this object into client props. No admin/suspension checks exist.

### Sending and current quota

`src/lib/actions.ts:submitCampaign()` calls `src/lib/campaigns.ts:createCampaign()`, then `dispatchPending()`. A failed event publication leaves durable database queue rows for maintenance. `createCampaign()` uses a transaction and `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `User`; validates owned templates/contacts/resumes, checks Gmail connection, skips pending recipients and previously sent addresses unless specifically authorized through `resendIds`, renders personalized snapshots, and assigns `<send [REDACTED_EMAIL]>` MIME IDs. `campaignSchema` in `src/lib/validation.ts` caps recipients at 10, with Free further limited to 3 by server entitlements.

`src/lib/email-limits.ts` currently sets `DAILY_EMAIL_LIMIT = 200`. `src/lib/delivery-usage.ts:countQuotaUsage()` counts successful sends and retained receipts in a **rolling 24 hours**, plus all queued/attempting/uncertain deliveries, regardless of queue age. There is no monthly limit, persisted period counter, or explicit reservation ledger. The worker also checks the quota; its `> DAILY_EMAIL_LIMIT` comparison deliberately includes the current already-queued email, so replacing it with a simplistic `>=` would incorrectly reject the last reserved slot.

`src/lib/inngest.ts:deliverOne()` claims READY sends under the user lock, records ATTEMPTING, and checks `nextSendAt`. It builds MIME with `src/lib/gmail.ts:buildMime()`, calls `gmail.users.messages.send`, and stores SENT/DONE, `sentAt`, and provider IDs. Gmail HTTP automatic retries are disabled. MIME has one `To`, no CC/BCC, plain text, and optional PDF; file/URL access is disabled in Nodemailer.

`sendEmail` / function ID `send-individual-email` listens for `mailloop/email.queued`, uses per-user concurrency 1, retries 3, durable sleeps, explicit throttle retries at 60/120/240 seconds, and uncertainty reconciliation. Pacing uses `User.nextSendAt`, an initial 60-second claim guard, and a randomized 20–60-second delay after attempts. Inngest retry counts and explicit retry-loop counts are different mechanisms.

### Delivery and reply tracking

`src/lib/inngest.ts:reconcile()` searches Sent using `messages.list` with `in:sent rfc822msgid:...`, then `messages.get(format: metadata)`. This needs read-capable permission. If delivery cannot be proven, the send remains UNCERTAIN and is not automatically resent; quota remains occupied even if status becomes FAILED.

`replyCandidates()` selects up to 50 sends, normally with an eight-hour cutoff. `checkOneReply()` calls `threads.get(format: metadata)` with From and Auto-Submitted headers. It checks recipient address, internal timestamp, Gmail ID, SENT label, and auto-response headers before setting REPLIED. It reads Gmail mailbox/thread metadata, including incoming messages, but does not persist incoming bodies. The permission remains broad. Failures currently return false, and `lastCheckedAt` is updated in `finally`, so that timestamp **does not prove a successful inbox check**.

There is no read receipt/open pixel, destination SMTP delivery guarantee, bounce parser, or Gmail push-history integration. SENT means Gmail accepted the API request, not that the recipient received it. “Full delivery tracking” must be defined honestly; even read access does not provide a universal delivered/opened signal.

### Jobs, existing follow-ups, UI, deletion, and security

- `src/app/api/inngest/route.ts` serves sendEmail, maintenance, refreshReplyJob, and scheduledReplies. Production depends on Inngest signature validation and `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`; development mode is explicitly excluded in production in `src/lib/inngest.ts`.
- `maintenance` runs each minute, pages IDs, dispatches pending sends, cleans attachments, and retries disabled-account deletion. `scheduledReplies` runs `0 */8 * * *` and fans out `mailloop/replies.refresh` for connected active users; there is no paid gate.
- `src/lib/follow-ups.ts:readFollowUps()` returns due reminders based on elapsed days, shortlist/history state, and recorded REPLIED sends. `saveFollowUpDays()` in `src/lib/launch-actions.ts` accepts 0/3/7/14. `Contact.followUpRequestedAt`, yellow recipients, and `resendIds` authorize **manual additional outreach**; there is no automatic scheduler or reply-threaded follow-up MIME.
- `src/lib/actions.ts` exposes template/contact save/archive, CSV import, preferences, shortlist controls, and reply refresh. CSV is available to all, accepts parsed input as well as text, and validates up to 1,000 rows. Custom role values are available in preferences, contacts, imports, and Compose overrides. Templates are unlimited.
- `src/app/api/quota/route.ts` returns `{used,limit:200}` with private/no-store; `src/lib/quota-usage.ts` memoizes only within a request. `src/components/workspace-quota.tsx` polls every minute/focus. Layout, Compose, History, Settings, tooltips, tutorial, terms, and landing copy contain the existing limits/claims. History's “today” begins at UTC midnight, inconsistent with its rolling quota today.
- `src/lib/crypto.ts` encrypts refresh tokens with AES-256-GCM, random 12-byte IV, authentication tag, and a `v1` envelope. `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` must be 64 hex characters. Encryption exists; key IDs/rotation support and operational key storage need improvement. Actual production key management was not verified.
- `src/lib/validation.ts` caps PDFs at 5 MiB and checks MIME/header magic. `src/lib/storage.ts` uses private Blob in production, owner-prefixed UUID paths, bounded reads, and restricted local storage in development. `src/app/api/resume/blob/route.ts` authenticates upload-token issuance and relies on the Blob SDK to verify completion callbacks.
- `src/lib/cancellation.ts` cancels only QUEUED/READY sends under the same user lock. Already-started/uncertain sends cannot be recalled. `src/lib/history.ts:clearCompletedHistory()` permanently removes eligible rows, transfers successful sends to receipts, and retains campaign submission keys.
- `src/lib/account.ts` already supports authenticated export/deletion. Deletion disables access immediately but **waits 90 days before token revocation, PDF cleanup, and database purge**. `DELETION_DRAIN_MS` is 15 minutes for late Blob callbacks; it is not the account purge deadline. No billing cancellation exists.
- `src/app/privacy/page.tsx` explicitly discloses read access, metadata tracking, nonautomatic reminders, and 90-day deletion. `src/app/terms/page.tsx` includes no-spam/suspension rights and existing sending limits but no subscription/refund policy.
- Existing Vitest, database integration, and desktop/mobile Playwright tests are substantial. `tests/quota.test.ts`, `tests/reply-schedule.test.ts`, `tests/integration.db.test.ts`, `tests/launch.db.test.ts`, `tests/history-migration.db.test.ts`, and account/storage tests are relevant. Database tests are opt-in and mutate fixtures; none were run for this planning task.

## 2. Conflicts and risks

### Gmail permissions and the promised product

Google classifies `gmail.send` as sensitive; `gmail.readonly` and even `gmail.metadata` as restricted. Server processing of restricted data brings additional verification/security-assessment requirements. Fetching metadata instead of bodies does not remove that classification. Assessment cost and review duration require a current assessor quote and Google review; there is no defensible fixed cost estimate here. [Google scope classifications](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes).

**The complete paid feature list and “never read the inbox” cannot both hold with the current architecture.** Split entitlement from granted capability:

| Capability                                 | Send-only/basic                                               | Full, separately consented tracking                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Queue/failed/cancelled/API accepted status | Available from application state                              | Same                                                                                              |
| Uncertain-send recovery                    | Manual review; conservatively occupy quota; never blind retry | Sent-message metadata reconciliation                                                              |
| Replies                                    | User manually marks replied                                   | Tracked-thread metadata checks; no stored incoming bodies                                         |
| Bounce knowledge                           | Explicit API rejection or manual mark bounced                 | Optional conservative DSN processing, requiring mailbox access and additional scope justification |
| Destination delivery/open guarantee        | Unavailable                                                   | Still unavailable universally; label evidence precisely                                           |

Remove `gmail.readonly` from initial OAuth only after adjusting the granted-scope check, Gmail connection UI, all scheduled/manual tracking paths, and ambiguous recovery. Store actual grants. Retiring an OAuth request scope does not revoke previously issued broad tokens: disable read calls, then plan revocation/reconsent for old users before claiming all grants are send-only. Optional read authorization should be incremental and validated against the same Google identity; cannot link another Gmail account accidentally.

### Stopping automatic follow-ups

| Option                                                   | Benefit                                       | Limitation/cost                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Manual “mark replied / do not contact / bounced”         | No inbox read scope; straightforward v1       | Users must act before scheduled send; cannot guarantee automatic reply-stop                                                                                                 |
| Opt-in `gmail.readonly` and tracked-thread polling       | Reuses current reply detection and recovery   | Restricted verification/assessment, consent, operational cost; polling delay/race; broad grant                                                                              |
| `gmail.metadata` and metadata-only thread/history checks | Less content visibility                       | Still restricted; search-query limitations affect Sent reconciliation; requires a separate recovery redesign                                                                |
| Reply-To to a Mailloop inbound address                   | App can receive replies without reading Gmail | Changes recipients' reply destination, processes incoming contents, requires inbound infrastructure; misses replies sent directly to original Gmail; not equivalent privacy |
| User-controlled Gmail forwarding                         | No Gmail read API permission                  | Setup friction, broader third-party processing, incomplete coverage; not recommended for v1                                                                                 |

Recommended: send-only v1, manual reply/opt-out controls immediately; launch reply-aware auto-follow-ups only after opt-in read verification. If manual-stop auto-sends are deliberately launched, present them as such and require per-sequence approval. Never say they automatically stop on replies. Even read polling cannot eliminate a reply arriving between the final check and Gmail submission; disclose this narrow race.

### Other code conflicts

- **Free follow-ups:** existing `resendIds`, re-saving contacts, and shortlist restoration can already send manual follow-ups. If “no follow-ups” includes manual repeat outreach, gate these at campaign creation and execution as well as the new auto feature. Default: it includes both. Free users retain read access to old contacts/history.
- **Custom roles:** hiding the Compose text box leaves `saveContact`, `savePreferences`, `importContacts`, and saved contact roles as bypasses. Define canonical roles in a server-shared module; check actual rendered role at send time. Do not attempt to police every word in user-composed bodies.
- **Quota races:** keep row locking across reservations, retries, cancellation, period changes, billing transitions, and admin mutations. Inngest concurrency alone cannot serialize different functions/manual actions or database backfills.
- **Gmail exactly-once:** a MIME Message-ID is not a provider idempotency key. A crash after Google accepts a message but before the DB commits is intrinsically ambiguous. Preserve UNCERTAIN, prevent automatic resend, and do not release a potentially consumed slot.
- **Downgrade in flight:** cancel/release unclaimed paid-only work; an already claimed external request may finish. Guards linearize at the claim instant; they cannot recall Gmail requests.
- **History deletion:** a new ledger must survive deleting a `Send`. Otherwise users can delete usage/duplicate evidence or cascade away scheduled-work state unintentionally.
- **Reply check failure:** replace boolean false with checked/no-reply/replied/failed outcomes and successful-check timestamp. Automated sends must pause on a failed check, not infer silence.
- **Template race:** two concurrent “first template” saves must share the owner lock. Read-only extra templates must also be excluded from Compose/API use, not merely disabled for editing.
- **Billing drift:** need provider subscription IDs and event history in addition to the four requested User fields; an email match is not a secure webhook-to-user mapping.
- **False delivery claims:** revise “delivery” copy and progress semantics. Follow-up suppression after a later bounce does not refund an email already accepted by Gmail.
- **Deletion and subscriptions:** leaving the existing 90-day cleanup sequence unchanged could continue charging an inaccessible account. Cancel billing promptly, independently of personal-data retention.
- **No refunds:** publish the chosen policy but have Dodo/legal review confirm mandatory consumer remedies, chargebacks, and provider-required refunds. A product rule cannot prevent a provider refund/dispute event.
- **₹299 economics:** verify tax-inclusive proceeds, fixed/per-payment/recurring/FX fees, Inngest/Blob costs, and restricted-scope assessment costs before charging. Do not assume $5.99 economics transfer to the India price.

## 3. Database changes

### Schema additions

These are exact proposed additions, **not an applied schema**. Preserve existing fields/relations and Prisma 7.10.0. Provider IDs remain provider strings; application primary keys remain UUID-generated strings consistent with existing PostgreSQL FK types. If native UUID columns are desired, make that a separate fully tested migration.

Add these fields/relations to existing `User`:

```prisma
plan                       Plan               @default(FREE)
subscriptionStatus         SubscriptionStatus @default(NONE)
currentPeriodStart         DateTime?
currentPeriodEnd           DateTime?
dodoCustomerId             String?            @unique
dodoSubscriptionId         String?            @unique
cancelAtPeriodEnd          Boolean            @default(false)
gracePeriodEnd             DateTime?
billingCountry             String?
billingCurrency            String?
billingStateVersion        Int                @default(0)
lastBillingEventAt         DateTime?
planOverride               Plan?
planOverrideStartsAt       DateTime?
planOverrideExpiresAt      DateTime?
planOverrideReason         String?
grandfatheredUntil         DateTime?
freeTemplateId             String?
isAdmin                    Boolean            @default(false)
isSuspended                Boolean            @default(false)
suspendedAt                DateTime?
suspensionReason           String?
lastActiveAt               DateTime?
googleGrantedScopes        String[]           @default([])
gmailReadAuthorized        Boolean            @default(false)
sendingPausedAt            DateTime?
sendingPauseReason         String?
sendingResumeAt            DateTime?
googleRevokedAt            DateTime?
billingCancelledAt         DateTime?
personalDataPurgedAt       DateTime?
subscriptions              BillingSubscription[]
checkoutAttempts           CheckoutAttempt[]
usagePeriods               UsagePeriod[]
usageReservations          UsageReservation[]
followUpSequences          FollowUpSequence[]
followUpSteps              FollowUpStep[]
adminActions               AdminAuditLog[]     @relation("AdminActor")

@@index([plan, subscriptionStatus, createdAt, id])
@@index([isSuspended, createdAt, id])
@@index([currentPeriodEnd])
@@index([gracePeriodEnd])
@@index([lastActiveAt])
```

`freeTemplateId` is deliberately an application-validated pointer like the existing `currentAttachmentId`: validate ownership/active state under the user lock on selection/use, and replace deterministically when archived. `plan` is the provider-derived base access plan; an override or transition benefit affects `effectivePlan`, not the stored provider status. `subscriptionStatus` preserves the provider lifecycle even after `plan` falls back to FREE.

Add to existing `Send`, keeping `SendStatus` and `DeliveryState` intact:

```prisma
kind                    EmailKind          @default(INITIAL)
quotaReservation        UsageReservation?
followUpStep            FollowUpStep?
rootedFollowUpSequence  FollowUpSequence?   @relation("FollowUpRoot")
replyDetectedAt         DateTime?
replySource             String?
lastSuccessfulCheckAt   DateTime?
bouncedAt               DateTime?
bounceSource            String?
failureCode             String?
availableAt             DateTime           @default(now())
queueExpiresAt          DateTime?
claimToken              String?
leaseExpiresAt          DateTime?
inReplyToMessageId       String?
referenceMessageIds     String[]           @default([])
entitlementVersion      Int                @default(1)

@@index([status, deliveryState, availableAt, id])
@@index([deliveryState, leaseExpiresAt])
```

Add `followUpSequences FollowUpSequence[]` to `Attachment`. `availableAt` is for safe retry/send-window scheduling; a due `FollowUpStep` is not yet a queued email. Existing manual resends must be backfilled/classified separately; `INITIAL` default alone must not allow free repeat sends.

```prisma
enum Plan {
  FREE
  PAID
}

enum SubscriptionStatus {
  NONE
  PENDING
  ACTIVE
  PAST_DUE
  ON_HOLD
  CANCELLED
  EXPIRED
  FAILED
  PAUSED
}

enum UsagePeriodKind {
  DAY
  MONTH
}

enum ReservationStatus {
  RESERVED
  ATTEMPTING
  UNCERTAIN
  CONFIRMED
  RELEASED
}

enum EmailKind {
  INITIAL
  MANUAL_FOLLOW_UP
  AUTO_FOLLOW_UP
}

enum FollowUpSequenceStatus {
  ACTIVE
  PAUSED
  COMPLETED
  CANCELLED
}

enum FollowUpStepStatus {
  SCHEDULED
  WAITING_QUOTA
  QUEUED
  SENT
  CANCELLED
  FAILED
}

model BillingSubscription {
  id                   String             @id @default(uuid())
  userId               String
  dodoSubscriptionId   String             @unique
  dodoCustomerId       String
  productId            String
  status               SubscriptionStatus
  periodStart          DateTime?
  periodEnd            DateTime?
  gracePeriodEnd       DateTime?
  cancelAtPeriodEnd    Boolean            @default(false)
  currency             String?
  billingCountry       String?
  recurringAmountMinor Int?
  lastEventAt          DateTime?
  createdAt            DateTime           @default(now())
  updatedAt            DateTime           @updatedAt
  user                 User               @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  @@index([status, periodEnd])
}

model CheckoutAttempt {
  id                 String    @id @default(uuid())
  userId             String
  idempotencyKey     String
  productId          String
  billingCountry     String
  billingCurrency    String
  dodoSessionId      String?   @unique
  status             String    @default("CREATING")
  expiresAt          DateTime
  createdAt          DateTime  @default(now())
  user               User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, idempotencyKey])
  @@index([userId, status, expiresAt])
}

model BillingWebhookEvent {
  id                 String    @id @default(uuid())
  webhookId          String    @unique
  eventType          String
  businessId         String
  subscriptionId     String?
  customerId         String?
  paymentId          String?
  occurredAt         DateTime
  receivedAt         DateTime  @default(now())
  processedAt        DateTime?
  nextAttemptAt      DateTime?
  attempts           Int       @default(0)
  processingVersion  Int       @default(1)
  state              String    @default("RECEIVED")
  normalizedData     Json
  payloadHash        String
  failureCode        String?

  @@index([state, nextAttemptAt, receivedAt])
  @@index([subscriptionId, occurredAt])
  @@index([customerId, occurredAt])
}

model UsagePeriod {
  id                   String          @id @default(uuid())
  userId               String
  kind                 UsagePeriodKind
  periodKey            String
  startsAt             DateTime
  endsAt               DateTime
  sent                 Int             @default(0)
  reserved             Int             @default(0)
  importedSent         Int             @default(0)
  importedUncertain    Int             @default(0)
  configVersion        Int             @default(1)
  createdAt            DateTime        @default(now())
  updatedAt            DateTime        @updatedAt
  user                 User            @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  dailyReservations    UsageReservation[] @relation("DailyUsage")
  monthlyReservations  UsageReservation[] @relation("MonthlyUsage")

  @@unique([userId, kind, periodKey])
  @@index([userId, kind, startsAt, endsAt])
}

model UsageReservation {
  id                  String            @id @default(uuid())
  userId              String
  deliveryKey         String            @unique
  sendId              String?           @unique
  dailyPeriodId       String
  monthlyPeriodId     String
  status              ReservationStatus @default(RESERVED)
  reservedAt          DateTime          @default(now())
  attemptedAt         DateTime?
  confirmedAt         DateTime?
  releasedAt          DateTime?
  leaseExpiresAt      DateTime?
  releaseReason       String?
  claimToken          String?
  user                User              @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  send                Send?             @relation(fields: [sendId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  dailyPeriod         UsagePeriod       @relation("DailyUsage", fields: [dailyPeriodId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  monthlyPeriod       UsagePeriod       @relation("MonthlyUsage", fields: [monthlyPeriodId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([userId, status, reservedAt])
  @@index([status, leaseExpiresAt])
  @@index([dailyPeriodId, status])
  @@index([monthlyPeriodId, status])
}

model FollowUpSequence {
  id                    String                 @id @default(uuid())
  userId                String
  rootSendId            String?                @unique
  recipientEmail        String
  status                FollowUpSequenceStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  delayDays             Int[]
  maxFollowUps          Int                    @default(2)
  minGapDays            Int                    @default(3)
  approvedAt            DateTime
  expiresAt             DateTime
  stopReason            String?
  stoppedAt             DateTime?
  requireAutomaticReplyCheck Boolean           @default(true)
  attachmentId          String?
  createdAt             DateTime               @default(now())
  user                  User                   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  rootSend              Send?                  @relation("FollowUpRoot", fields: [rootSendId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  attachment            Attachment?            @relation(fields: [attachmentId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  steps                 FollowUpStep[]

  @@index([userId, status, recipientEmail])
  @@index([status, expiresAt])
}

model FollowUpStep {
  id                    String             @id @default(uuid())
  userId                String
  sequenceId            String
  stepNumber            Int
  delayDays             Int
  dueAt                 DateTime?
  status                FollowUpStepStatus @default(SCHEDULED)
  sendId                String?            @unique
  subject               String
  body                  String
  lastReplyCheckAt       DateTime?
  stopReason            String?
  createdAt             DateTime           @default(now())
  user                  User               @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  sequence              FollowUpSequence   @relation(fields: [sequenceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  send                  Send?              @relation(fields: [sendId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@unique([sequenceId, stepNumber])
  @@index([userId, status, dueAt])
  @@index([status, dueAt, id])
}

model AdminAuditLog {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid())
  actorUserId       String?
  targetUserId      String?
  actorIdSnapshot   String
  targetIdSnapshot  String?
  action            String
  requestId         String   @unique
  reason            String
  before            Json
```

## 5. Quota enforcement design

### Invariants and periods

Use explicit counters **and** a reservation ledger. `sent + reserved` cannot exceed the active limit when authorizing new work, though a downgrade may make historical consumption exceed the new cap. Each deliveryKey has at most one reservation and can confirm/release once. Counters and transitions commit atomically. Ledger rows do not disappear with history. An UNCERTAIN send retains capacity because absence of evidence is not proof it was unsent.

- Daily key `day:2026-10-13`, [00:00 UTC, next 00:00 UTC).
- Free monthly key `free:2026-10`, [first day 00:00 UTC, next first day).
- Paid monthly key `paid:<subscriptionId>:<verified periodStart ISO>`; boundaries come from signed provider `previous_billing_date` / `next_billing_date`, not a guessed 30 days. Store UTC instants.
- Complimentary paid override uses explicitly defined UTC calendar-month buckets, not fictitious provider cycles. Paid subscribers under an override continue using their provider period.
- New rows are created lazily using the unique key; no job zeros an existing counter. No rollover. Treat the quota day as the UTC day **the Gmail send attempt starts**, so a bounded in-flight request crossing midnight stays attributed to its claim. Explain this operational definition in help; an accepted email's display timestamp may differ by seconds.
- Maintain one logical monthly allowance, not an additive free + paid allowance. On free→paid activation, seed the first paid bucket with consumption since its exact start and exclude legitimate earlier free sends. On paid→free downgrade, seed the calendar bucket from all confirmed/uncertain attempts in that month, including paid attempts and receipts; e.g. 100 paid sends this calendar month leaves zero free sends. Daily bucket is shared across plans and never resets on upgrade/downgrade. Repeated override/subscription toggles must not issue new monthly credit.
- Later-overlapping period materialization seeds from surviving reservations/ledger plus imported historical evidence; never just starts at zero if sends occurred in its window. Baseline imports and ledger increments must be disjoint. Historical reservations stay attributed to their original bucket; imported baselines count overlapping sends when a different entitlement window is created.

### Step-by-step queue and execution

1. **Queue:** `createCampaign()` locks User, reloads effective entitlements, validates contacts/template/roles, deduplicates submission via current `(userId,idempotencyKey)`, and obtains daily/monthly bucket rows. For N selected emails, require both `sent + reserved + N <= limit`. Create Campaign, Send snapshots, and one reservation per Send in the same transaction; increment each bucket's `reserved` by N. If either cap fails, queue none and return the blocking period/remaining capacity. Client checks are advisory.
2. **Outbox:** commit first, then publish Inngest `send-<sendId>`. Existing maintenance repairs failed publication. Event IDs improve dispatch dedupe but do not replace database reservation keys. Update `dispatchPending()` to respect availableAt, suspension and feature flags; add repair for dispatched READY jobs that never started after a safe timeout, with database no-duplicate guards.
3. **Worker check:** event contains only owner/send IDs. Reload/validate owner; reject cross-user rows, deletion, suspension, global kill switch, missing required scopes, invalid follow-up, or expired access. Under the User lock check current Send and reservation state. A confirmed/released terminal row or completed Send is a no-op. A malformed event never calls Gmail.
4. **Period crossing:** queued READY work must not spend yesterday's reservation to evade today's cap. Before claim, atomically decrement old reserved counters and increment destination counters/update reservation pointers **only if** destination has capacity. If capacity is unavailable, retain its old reservation, do not send, and wait until a eligible boundary or queue expiry; old reserved capacity is not usable new-day credit. Retrying the transaction checks fresh current periods. Normal queue expiry defaults to 24 elapsed hours from queueing; confirmed unattempted expired work is cancelled/released. Follow-ups waiting on quota stay as FollowUpStep WAITING_QUOTA without a Send/reservation until they can actually queue. Avoid thousands of sleeping quota-retry steps by maintenance redispatch.
5. **Final claim:** after expensive token refresh/attachment preparation, re-enter the short transaction and recheck access, quota binding, global/per-user state, and fresh reply evidence if required. CAS READY/RESERVED→ATTEMPTING with a random UUID claim token and bounded lease (two minutes initially, greater than transport timeout). Reserve `nextSendAt`. Do not perform external network requests while holding SQL row locks. Worker concurrency 1 plus the owner lock remains in place across initial and follow-up sends.
6. **Send:** submit one MIME message; same stable Message-ID for the logical Send, no CC/BCC. Mark internally when the request could have reached Google. Google does not offer an exactly-once transaction with this database.
7. **Confirm:** under the same owner lock/CAS and claim token, persist provider IDs/SENT/DONE and reservation CONFIRMED together. Decrement both reserved counts and increment both sent counts once. Reply/bounce status later does not double-count, refund, or move successful quota. Schedule sequence next step only after successful commit.
8. **Release:** for cancellation before submission, proven permanent rejection, missing/invalid attachment before Gmail, exhausted safe throttle retries, or queue expiry while READY, atomically mark RELEASED and decrement both reserved counts once. Store a reason code. Completed history deletion preserves ledger/receipt safeguards. Released terminal Sends cannot be restarted by replaying an old event; a new explicit campaign gets a new key.
9. **Safe retries:** pre-submission failures and explicit temporary Google rejections preserve reservation; return to READY with next availability, respecting backoff/pacing. Do not make a second reservation. SQL deadlock/serialization conflicts retry the short transaction with bounded jitter, not the Gmail submission. See section 15 for detailed provider classification.
10. **Ambiguous outcome:** timeout/socket failure/5xx after possible submission or a DB failure after accepted response → UNCERTAIN, retain counters, never automatically resend. With read consent, reconcile Sent metadata by Message-ID and confirm if found. With send-only, display manual review; user may mark “found in Sent” to finalize conservatively. “I cannot find it” alone should not automatically refund or resend. Admin resolution needs evidence and an audit; default uncertain consumption remains charged to its original attempt period and ages out of current-period remaining quota at the normal boundary, while its duplicate-protection state survives.

Use a consistent lock order: User → daily bucket → monthly bucket → Send/reservation (stable ordering when moving old/new buckets). Billing/admin lifecycle updates use the User lock too. Fetch all fresh user/global controls within the claim transaction; a kill switch that wins after claim cannot undo an already authorized in-flight Gmail call. Do not reuse an Inngest memoized entitlement decision across sleeps or attempts.

### Grace and late renewal

At PAST_DUE, keep the previous paid allowance and its usage through the grace deadline; do not allocate another 300 automatically. Extend that bucket's operational endsAt to gracePeriodEnd, while User.currentPeriodEnd remains the original provider billing boundary. If a signed renewal later establishes a new paid period beginning inside the grace window, seed its allowance with attempts already made in that new window. That is usage attribution, not a second quota reset. Daily limits remain unchanged. If provider snapshots are missing at expiry, pause new paid sends while repairing state; do not grant infinite grace. A real failed-renewal downgrade activates the free calendar allowance with paid consumption included.

### Reconciliation job

Add `quota-reconciliation` (every five minutes) in `src/lib/inngest.ts`, registered in `src/app/api/inngest/route.ts`. Page IDs only, then operate by owner under locks. Repair:

- RESERVED + READY past queue expiry or already CANCELLED/proven-unsent FAILED: release once.
- RESERVED without a Send due to history deletion: normal history deletion must only remove terminal rows; unexpected outstanding orphans need alert/investigation, not blind release.
- ATTEMPTING lease expiry: convert to UNCERTAIN, try consented recovery; **do not release merely because a lease expired**.
- SENT/REPLIED with unconfirmed ledger: confirm once using accepted-response evidence; never resubmit.
- CONFIRMED ledger with deleted Send: valid; preserve usage.
- READY undispatched/stuck-dispatched: safely republish with same logical key and recheck before send.
- Counter drift: recompute `sent = importedSent + CONFIRMED ledger count`; `reserved = importedUncertain + RESERVED/ATTEMPTING/UNCERTAIN ledger count`, with ownership and period predicates. Report discrepancies and repair inside locks.

Alert on uncertainty older than 15 minutes, unpublished queues older than five minutes, unexplained drift, and repair failures. Prevent one broken owner from blocking all maintenance. Signed/provider/API errors, minimal manual review, and imported exception baselines need operational visibility without message contents.

## 7. Subscription lifecycle

Provider state, effective access, admin overrides, suspension and Google capability are distinct. Store requested plan/status/period/customer fields on User as a projection, plus historical BillingSubscription records. Read effective access using current time even if an expiry job is delayed.

| Current state / trigger              | Next state and effective access                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Signup                               | FREE / NONE, calendar usage, optional published transition benefit only for prelaunch users.                                                      |
| Start checkout                       | Pending CheckoutAttempt; existing User access stays unchanged. New subscriber may have PENDING status; no PAID from redirect.                     |
| Verified activation                  | PAID / ACTIVE, current provider period; clear old grace/failure markers.                                                                          |
| Cancel scheduled                     | PAID / ACTIVE + cancelAtPeriodEnd; paid access through currentPeriodEnd.                                                                          |
| Revoke scheduled cancel              | PAID / ACTIVE, flag false after signed update. Same allowance, no reset.                                                                          |
| Verified renewal                     | PAID / ACTIVE, next actual cycle; distinct bucket, no unused rollover.                                                                            |
| Renewal fails                        | PAID / PAST_DUE through signed grace deadline; usage continues without extra 300.                                                                 |
| Recovery within grace                | PAID / ACTIVE, provider dates; count intervening sends in the proper recovered window.                                                            |
| Grace expires / ON_HOLD              | FREE / ON_HOLD; provider account remains recoverable; show portal payment update.                                                                 |
| Ordinary scheduled cancellation ends | FREE / CANCELLED; old subscription retained.                                                                                                      |
| Term expires / initial failure       | FREE / EXPIRED or FAILED; new checkout needed.                                                                                                    |
| Recovery after hold                  | PAID / ACTIVE only on provider confirmation; do not resurrect cancelled old automation.                                                           |
| Re-subscribe after cancellation      | New provider subscription; old events update historical row but cannot overwrite current projection.                                              |
| Suspension                           | Sending disabled immediately independent of paid status; still allow billing cancellation, data export/delete and support.                        |
| Admin override                       | Effective plan overlaid until explicit expiry; provider state unchanged; audit before/after. No override creates charges or bypasses kill switch. |
| Account deletion                     | Disable sending/access, cancel outstanding work and billing promptly; delete data on retention schedule.                                          |

At downgrade, under User lock:

1. Select/free-lock templates; retain all content. One usable/editable free template; extras read-only/exportable, not deleted. Restore them on upgrade.
2. Cancel all scheduled auto-follow-up sequences and unclaimed follow-up Send rows; release their slots. They do not resume merely on re-subscribe.
3. Revalidate queued initial emails against free caps/features/current periods. Cancel READY campaigns with templates outside the current plan or more than three initially approved recipients; default cancel the unsent remainder of that invalid campaign and notify, rather than silently choose recipients. Smaller compliant campaigns can proceed only when free remaining quota fits. Already claimed sends may finish and count; never refund UNCERTAIN slots.
4. Stop full reply polling; retain existing detected reply labels/manual stop controls. Read-based uncertain recovery, if allowed after downgrade, must be restricted to previously submitted sends and disclosed; recommend manual review when using the strict free send-only contract.
5. CSV-imported contacts remain owned/readable; imported origin does not require deleting them. Free new sends must use canonical roles and eligible templates. Paid history remains viewable.
6. Show “Free access starts …”, limits/usage and lock explanations. Grace expiry includes paid sends in the free calendar bucket, so remaining may be zero until reset.

Separate ordinary paid-access cancellation from exceptional immediate account termination (fraud/dispute/service action). No app admin plan override implicitly cancels the provider subscription; show an explicit warning if someone is still being billed while access is overridden down. Suspension billing policy must be approved; recommended schedule cancellation promptly on abuse suspension so the account is not renewed indefinitely.

## 8. Auto follow-up feature design

### Approval and scheduling

FollowUpSequence is per original Send/recipient, with approvedAt, frozen recipient, chosen delays, expiry and stop policy. FollowUpStep stores the user-approved personalized body/subject, step number, chosen delay and computed dueAt. These are email contents and must never appear in admin/logs/Inngest event payloads. Default allow 1–2 follow-ups, seven elapsed days between messages; choices 3/7/14, minimum three. A second dueAt is based on the previous **actual successful send**, not the original ideal schedule, so quota/pacing delays cannot compress gaps. A two-times-14-day sequence fits a 30-day lifetime; later delays may expire it.

Paid user explicitly enables auto-send on Compose, previews each follow-up/attachment, chooses delay options, and acknowledges sends consume the same 20/day and 300/period allowance. Original send and approval snapshot persist together, but future follow-ups do not reserve today's quota weeks ahead. Start sequence only after confirmed original send. No automatic activation of current `followUpDays` reminders.

Add `follow-up-dispatcher` cron every five minutes that owner-pages due SCHEDULED/WAITING_QUOTA steps, and `follow-up-due` event with userId/sequenceId/stepId only. Durable `step.sleepUntil` may handle near-term dueAt; the table and dispatcher remain the source of truth/recovery, with CAS status preventing duplicate wakes. Do not hold the main send concurrency slot during multi-day sleeps. The due worker queues an ordinary `Send(kind:AUTO_FOLLOW_UP)` through shared reservation logic, then all actual sending uses `send-individual-email` so initial/follow-up pacing is shared.

Quota shortage: step stays WAITING_QUOTA, gets a displayed reason, and is tried after the next daily reset or verified monthly boundary while access/expiry permits. No new reservation until queued. Do not silently burst deferred follow-ups at reset: same pacing/window governs them. Stop at 30-day expiry or 48 hours of failed required reply verification (default); manual user review can deliberately restart a new sequence.

### Threading

Extend `buildMime()` with `inReplyTo` and `references`, supply stored original/previous RFC Message-ID values. Keep a stable matching subject for the thread (test `Re:` handling; using the original exact subject is safest initially), original recipient snapshot, and saved `gmailThreadId` in `messages.send({requestBody:{raw,threadId}})`. The next step's In-Reply-To points to the previous accepted outbound Message-ID; References contains the original and preceding message IDs. Gmail's required thread criteria are thread ID, RFC-compatible headers, and matching subject. [Gmail threading requirements](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/threads).

Sending with stored threadId does not require reading that thread first. If the thread ID is missing/original is uncertain, stop and require review; do not send a new standalone automatic message as a silent fallback. Never use only the Gmail API message ID as an RFC Message-ID.

### Stop checks and safeguards

- Before due processing **and immediately before Gmail claim**, check effective paid plan, auto feature flag, user not suspended/deleting/paused, sequence status, max steps, expiry and minimum gap. Check replies against the entire original thread/root, not just the newest follow-up timestamp; a reply to the original stops later steps too.
- In reply-aware mode, run a fresh metadata check just before submission. Require a successful check within 60 seconds of the final claim; repeat if token/attachment preparation exceeded that interval. Record successful outcome; fetch failure/invalid token/unknown thread means **pause, do not send**. Current eight-hour polling alone is insufficient. Stop on positive reply, including conservative handling of alternate reply aliases/unmatched inbound messages that may be the recipient; ambiguous evidence pauses for review.
- Manual “mark replied” creates replyDetectedAt/replySource and cancels all matching recipient sequences under the User lock; this works for both plans.
- User cancel, downgrade, suspension, account deletion, root-history deletion, or expiry cancels unclaimed steps/sends and releases slots. No restart by old event/re-subscription. Already ATTEMPTING/UNCERTAIN cannot be recalled/refunded without evidence.
- Detected bounce suppresses; out-of-office/Auto-Submitted pauses automation for review rather than counting as a human reply or continuing indefinitely. No opt-out-content classifier in v1 unless separately scoped/read-consented and tested; users need a manual opt-out control.
- One ACTIVE/PAUSED sequence per owner/address, two follow-ups total per root even if settings are edited; explicit resend does not bypass the minimum gap. Sequence approval does not authorize arbitrary later body edits by server automation.
- Default follow-ups have no reattached resume; if enabled by user, freeze an attachment FK and extend `cleanupAttachments()` to protect ACTIVE/PAUSED sequences. Deleting a resume or root history cancels dependent future auto-sends and cleans up unused snapshots/files.

Mark root REPLIED and cancel sequence in one owner transaction. Different Inngest function concurrency keys do not replace this check. Be explicit that a response arriving just after final verification can still cross with a message already submitted.

### Gmail retry/permanent-fail policy

Use Google HTTP status **and reason**; avoid assuming all 403 or 429 failures mean the same thing. Standard limits also include sends done directly in Gmail and other clients. [Google error handling](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/handle-errors).

| Outcome                                                                                  | Retry/pause policy                                                                                                                                                                       | Reservation policy                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Local validation, attachment missing/oversize before Gmail                               | Permanent failure, show actionable reason                                                                                                                                                | Release; definitely not submitted.                                                                                                       |
| OAuth `invalid_grant` / revoked refresh token                                            | Pause owner's sending and read jobs; gmailAuthorized=false; reconnect required. Cancel unclaimed queue by default, retain approved sequence as paused only until expiry/user reapproval. | Release proven unsubmitted cancelled emails; keep attempting/uncertain until resolved.                                                   |
| 401                                                                                      | Try one bounded fresh credential refresh when safe; if repeated/invalid grant, reconnect pause                                                                                           | Do not reserve twice; failed rejected attempt can release on final cancellation.                                                         |
| 403 `rateLimitExceeded` / `userRateLimitExceeded`, explicit 429 throttle rejection       | Honor Retry-After; exponential backoff with jitter and shared owner cooldown; bounded attempts (e.g. 5) / 24-hour queue lifetime                                                         | Preserve while retrying, release only final proven rejection/expiry.                                                                     |
| 429 mail-sending daily limit / long provider retry time                                  | Pause owner until provider retry time, otherwise conservative hours-scale cooldown; show Gmail limit, not app quota                                                                      | Release if queue expires before safe retry and no submission was accepted. Do not reroute through other Google accounts to evade limits. |
| 403 `dailyLimitExceeded` / project quota exhaustion                                      | Global operational alert/cooldown, distinguish Google project from user allowance                                                                                                        | Keep unsubmitted reservations during bounded pause; cancel/release expired READY work.                                                   |
| 403 insufficientPermissions / domainPolicy                                               | Reconnect for missing consent, workspace-admin instructions for domain policy; no rapid retries                                                                                          | Release final explicit rejection; stop queued work with actionable pause.                                                                |
| Explicit 400 malformed MIME/invalid recipient, 404 invalid thread, rejected message size | Permanent; stop offending sequence/thread fallback needs user review                                                                                                                     | Release if provider explicitly rejected submission.                                                                                      |
| Network/5xx before any submission (token refresh/read/prepare)                           | Safe bounded retry; required reply read failure pauses auto-send                                                                                                                         | Preserve until retry/expiry; no outgoing ambiguity yet.                                                                                  |
| Network/timeout/5xx during/after send, or DB commit failure after accepted response      | UNCERTAIN, Sent reconcile if permitted; no blind retry                                                                                                                                   | Keep reserved/consume conservatively; no lease-based refund.                                                                             |
| Gmail API accepted, later hard bounce                                                    | Record evidence, suppress/cancel future outreach                                                                                                                                         | Confirmed slot remains consumed.                                                                                                         |

Use `sendingPauseReason` codes such as RECONNECT_REQUIRED, PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT, PROVIDER_DAILY_LIMIT, DOMAIN_POLICY and SECURITY_SUSPENSION; only authorized reconnection clears credential pauses. Reconnection does not reactivate cancelled emails or increase quota. Read APIs can use safe transient retries; outgoing sends require stronger ambiguity handling than a generic SDK retry wrapper.

### Additional issues found during audit

- **One-off pass/annual quota:** do not conflate access expiry with quota month. A 30-day pass has one 300-email window; annual access needs 12 calendar/anchor monthly allowances. Add only when product decision is made.
- **Provider fees/minimums:** validate ₹299 in a real India-recurring quote with tax/FX/fees, and cost per retained paid customer. Do not implement discounted “pay what you want” as country validation.
- **Remote duplicate subscriptions:** local dedupe cannot fully eliminate unknown remote outcomes. Nightly reconcile all owned provider subscriptions; alert if more than one current recurring subscription, prevent another checkout, resolve billing rather than silently choosing one.
- **History erasure and scheduling:** clearing root history currently deletes follow-up reminders. Future cleanup must cancel approved sequences and erase follow-up bodies while preserving minimal usage/dedupe records. Never retain message bodies hidden behind a “delete history” operation.
- **Activity writes/pool pressure:** adding writes on every poll plus counter locks can overload the existing five-connection pool. Throttle lastActiveAt; bound page size/job fanout, keep locks short, and monitor queue latency before increasing connection counts.
- **Read permission retirement:** revocation can invalidate the sending token too; plan a deliberate reconnect flow. Disable read jobs before scope-policy claims, but don't assume an old token was downscoped merely because auth request text changed.
- **Support/admin accounting:** distinguish billed paid users from overrides and grandfathered accounts, record override expiry/reason, and show when access is denied but billing is still active. No staff access to Gmail or resumes to troubleshoot delivery.
- **Consent/change notice:** auto-send and payment terms require clear effective dates and user approval; existing reminder preferences cannot authorize new automatic mail. Store approval time/sequence snapshots and update privacy/terms before rollout.

The critical launch gates are reliable quota transactions, signed durable billing updates, truthful tracking/automation claims, revocable encrypted Google credentials, prompt subscription cancellation on deletion, and server-side suspension/admin controls. Everything else can be phased without sacrificing those guarantees.
